```{python Navigation header, results='asis'}
import os
import sys

sys.path.append("..")
import report_utils as ru
from IPython.display import display, HTML, Markdown

display(HTML(f"<div style='margin-bottom: 20px;'>{ru.nav_bar('reference')}</div>"))
```

## Introduction

Neither PMCMC nor ABC has an analytic target on the SIR model, so this report
builds one numerically. The particle-filter log-likelihood is evaluated on a
lattice over the prior box, replicates are combined with `logmeanexp`, the flat
log-prior is added, and the result is normalized by the cell area. The `pmcmc`
and `abc` reports both read the CSV produced here.

**What this reference can and cannot do.** It runs pypomp's own particle filter
on pypomp's own model, so it is *blind* to errors in the SIR translation: a
wrong model would produce a wrong reference that a wrong PMCMC would match
perfectly. It is the only **absolute** test that a sampler targets the posterior
implied by this model and prior. Detecting model errors is the job of the R
cross-check, and of the pfilter-logLik precondition that gates it — see the
PMCMC report.

A reference is only a reference to the extent its own Monte Carlo error is
small, so that error is reported below alongside the surface.

## The posterior surface

```{python Surface}
if have_grid:
    surface = grid.copy()
    # The dynamic range spans hundreds of nats, so plot on the log scale and
    # floor it well below the mode -- a linear scale shows one bright cell.
    floor = surface["log_post"].max() - 30.0
    surface["log_post_clipped"] = surface["log_post"].clip(lower=floor)
    display(
        ggplot(surface, aes(x="beta1", y="rho", fill="log_post_clipped"))
        + geom_raster()
        + labs(
            title="Reference log posterior density",
            subtitle="Clipped 30 nats below the mode; the true theta is marked",
            x="beta1",
            y="rho",
            fill="log density",
        )
        + ru.theme_premium
    )
else:
    display(Markdown("_No grid on disk._"))
```

```{python Truth and mode}
if have_grid:
    truth = pd.read_csv("../data/true_theta.csv")
    truth = dict(zip(truth["parameter"], truth["value"]))
    best = grid.loc[grid["log_post"].idxmax()]
    summary = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            {"quantity": "true beta1", "value": truth["beta1"]},
            {"quantity": "grid mode beta1", "value": float(best["beta1"])},
            {"quantity": "true rho", "value": truth["rho"]},
            {"quantity": "grid mode rho", "value": float(best["rho"])},
        ]
    )
    display(HTML(summary.to_html(
        classes="table table-striped table-hover", index=False, float_format="%.4f"
    )))
```

The grid mode is the maximum over cell centres, so it is quantized to the grid
spacing and is not expected to land exactly on the truth even for a perfect
reference. Posterior *mass* covering the truth is the meaningful check, and that
is made in the PMCMC report where credible intervals are available.

## Marginals

```{python Marginals}
if have_grid:
    frames = []
    for param, other in (("beta1", "rho"), ("rho", "beta1")):
        axis, dens = ru.grid_marginals(grid, param, other)
        frames.append(pd.DataFrame({"value": axis, "density": dens, "parameter": param}))

    for frame in frames:
        param = frame["parameter"].iloc[0]
        display(
            ggplot(frame, aes(x="value", y="density"))
            + geom_line(color=ru.color_palette["reference"], size=1)
            + geom_vline(xintercept=truth[param], color=ru.color_palette["truth"],
                         linetype="dashed")
            + labs(
                title=f"Reference marginal posterior: {param}",
                subtitle="Dashed line is the simulating value",
                x=param,
                y="density",
            )
            + ru.theme_premium
        )
```

## Monte Carlo error of the reference

Each grid point is a `logmeanexp` over replicate particle filters. The spread of
those replicates bounds how much of the surface's structure is noise rather than
signal. If this is comparable to the log-density differences between neighbouring
cells, the grid is under-resolved and `NREPS_REF`, `NP_REF`, or `GRID_N` should
be raised before the reference is trusted.

```{python MC error}
if have_grid and grid["logLik_sd"].notna().any():
    err = grid["logLik_sd"].dropna()
    stats = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            {"quantity": "median replicate sd (nats)", "value": err.median()},
            {"quantity": "max replicate sd (nats)", "value": err.max()},
            {
                "quantity": "log-density range across grid (nats)",
                "value": grid["log_post"].max() - grid["log_post"].min(),
            },
        ]
    )
    display(HTML(stats.to_html(
        classes="table table-striped table-hover", index=False, float_format="%.3f"
    )))
elif have_grid:
    display(Markdown(
        "_Only one replicate per grid point at this run level, so no Monte "
        "Carlo error estimate is available. Run at level 2 or above._"
    ))
```

## Resolution

```{python Resolution}
if have_grid:
    n_side = int(np.sqrt(len(grid)))
    b_axis = np.sort(grid["beta1"].unique())
    r_axis = np.sort(grid["rho"].unique())
    # Posterior sd from the gridded marginals, for a cells-per-sd figure.
    rows = []
    for param, other, axis in (("beta1", "rho", b_axis), ("rho", "beta1", r_axis)):
        ax, dens = ru.grid_marginals(grid, param, other)
        w = np.gradient(ax)
        mean = np.sum(ax * dens * w)
        sd = np.sqrt(np.sum((ax - mean) ** 2 * dens * w))
        spacing = float(np.mean(np.diff(axis)))
        rows.append(
            {
                "parameter": param,
                "posterior sd": sd,
                "grid spacing": spacing,
                "cells per sd": sd / spacing if spacing else np.nan,
            }
        )
    display(HTML(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_html(
        classes="table table-striped table-hover", index=False, float_format="%.4f"
    )))
    display(Markdown(
        f"Grid is {n_side}x{n_side}. Fewer than about two cells per posterior "
        "standard deviation means the marginals above are visibly discretized "
        "and the KS comparisons in the sampler reports will be dominated by "
        "grid resolution rather than by sampler error."
    ))
```
